title: Reversal of Towing and Labor Coverage Benefit Payments: Questions and Answers
content:
A **Towing and Labor Coverage** benefit payment is reversed at most once. Reversals are made for a duplicate invoice, a service not performed, or an ineligible service, for the full payment; a disablement reversed in full no longer counts toward the term maximum. The rule is the same on every Cardinal Point Towing and Labor package ($50 through $200).

## Questions and answers

**For what reasons is a towing and labor benefit reversed?**
For a duplicate invoice, for a service not performed, or for an ineligible service.

| Reason for reversal | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Duplicate invoice | The same service was invoiced more than once |
| Service not performed | The service paid for was not performed |
| Ineligible service | The service paid for was not eligible under the coverage |

**How much is reversed?**
The full payment. A reversal is for the whole amount of the benefit payment it reverses.

**How many times can one payment be reversed?**
At most once. The company's benefit records are checked for a reversal already booked against that same payment; where one exists, the payment is not reversed again.

**What happens to the term count when a payment is reversed?**
A disablement reversed in full no longer counts toward the term maximum of the vehicle's package.

**What happens to the benefits recorded on the coverage?**
They are the benefits paid less reversals, so a reversal reduces them by the amount reversed.

## Illustration (hypothetical inputs)

A benefit of $60.00 was paid to a network provider under one service reference, and the invoice is found to be a duplicate.

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| Reason | Duplicate invoice |
| Amount reversed | $60.00, the full payment |
| Benefits recorded on the coverage | Reduced by $60.00 |
| That disablement toward the term maximum | No longer counts |
| A second reversal of the same $60.00 payment | Not made |
